claims.text: Rapid liquid phase-assisted ultrahigh-temperature sintering can overcome the strength, structural-integrity, oxidation, and liquid-metal-corrosion limitations of single-phase ZrB2.
The proposed process is applicable at 1800 °C with a 30-minute hold.
The proposed process is applicable in an inert atmosphere under 50 MPa uniaxial pressure.
Rapid liquid-phase-assisted sintering increases densification of ZrB2.
Rapid liquid-phase-assisted sintering refines the ZrB2 grain structure.
The liquid phase enhances diffusion during rapid sintering.
The liquid phase enhances mass transport during rapid sintering.
Enhanced diffusion and mass transport produce an improved microstructure and improved properties.
The proposed material will exhibit a 25% increase in strength relative to single-phase ZrB2 prepared at 2300 °C and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The proposed material will exhibit a 30% improvement in oxidation resistance relative to single-phase ZrB2 prepared at 2300 °C and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The proposed material will exhibit a 40% reduction in liquid-plating-metal corrosion rate relative to single-phase ZrB2 prepared at 2300 °C and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The process is applicable at preparation temperatures below 2000 °C.
The resulting body is suitable for service at temperatures up to 1500 °C in a liquid plating bath.
Residual porosity may affect the predicted performance.
Impurities may affect the predicted performance.
